name: Keap
summary: CRM, sales and marketing automation built for small businesses. Capture leads, automate follow-up and manage your pipeline in one place.
best_for: service-based small businesses, coaches and solopreneurs who want CRM, email, payments and automation in one tool, and will invest the time to learn it
skip_if: you're price-sensitive, want a modern UI, or only need simple email: the cost and learning curve bite
honest_knock: Cost is the big one (56% of reviewers flag it), the interface feels dated, and there's a real 2–4 week learning curve on the automation builder. Billing and cancellation complaints are common: their own terms carry a $299 early termination fee on an annual contract and require ten days' phone notice, and email design is thinner than dedicated email tools.

pricing.notes: Starting at $299/mo billed monthly for the whole platform, with no feature-based tiers and no free plan (re-verified 2026-09-24 on their own pricing page; amounts unchanged since 5 September). That $299 is what the calculator quotes for its own minimum: 2 users and 1,500 contacts. Raising only the contact count on the same calculator gives $335 at 2,500, $449 at 5,000, $539 at 10,000 and $719 at 25,000, and users beyond the first two are $39 a month each. Keap also requires paid implementation services — strategy consulting, data import and migration — quoted separately before you go live. Text marketing is bundled at Tier 1 (500 messages and 100 voice minutes) and steps to $24, $39, $79, $139 and $279 a month above that, with overages at $0.015 a message and $0.01 a voice minute; it is US-only. Cancelling an annual contract before its term ends carries a $299 early termination fee, and cancellation must be started by phone at least ten days before the next invoice date. Keap has been acquired by Thryv; its own pages now route training to Thryv Academy.
